title: A protein sequence containing a `*` stop codon fails to parse
body:
A user reported that a protein fasta containing `*`, the IUPAC symbol for a stop codon, stops nail during seeding with this error:

```text
indexing query database... done (0.01s)
indexing target database... done (0.01s)
seeding...

error: progessive seeding failed

Caused by:
0: failed to write mmseqs target DB
1: failed to parse record
2: byte: "42" is not in the compressed amino acid alphabet
```

`Sequence::from_fasta` in `libnail/src/structs/sequence.rs` maps each residue byte through `UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO_TABLE`. It bails on any byte that maps to `UNKNOWN_UTF8_BYTE`, and `*` is one of those. The message gives the byte as a decimal number and names neither the record nor the file. The record fails only when nail writes the mmseqs target DB, after indexing has already reported success.

## Proposal

Read how HMMER and Easel handle `*` in a protein sequence, and match that behaviour as closely as nail can. The minimum is that a `*` at the end of a record parses without an error. An internal `*` may deserve a warning that names the record, for example "internal stop codon detected".

## Open

- how HMMER digitizes `*`, whether it treats a terminal `*` differently from an internal one, and what it scores at that position
- whether mmseqs accepts `*` in the sequence DB nail writes, or nail has to strip or replace it first
- whether the error for any other byte outside the alphabet should name the record and print the character; nail-d551f7 surveys errors like this one
